Bug_Title: ICAST: Integral value cast to double and then passed to Math.ceil (ICAST_INT_CAST_TO_DOUBLE_PASSED_TO_CEIL)
Bug_Details:
This code converts an integral value (e.g., int or long)
to a double precision
floating point number and then
passing the result to the Math.ceil() function, which rounds a double to
the next higher integer value. This operation should always be a no-op,
since converting an integer to a double should give a number with no fractional part.
It is likely that the operation that generated the value to be passed
to Math.ceil was intended to be performed using double precision
floating point arithmetic.
Bug_Explanation: The bug is embedded in the'showBug' method where an integer value is cast to a double and then passed to the Math.ceil() function, which should always be a no-op as converting an integer to a double should give a number with no fractional part.
Trigger_Explanation: The bug is triggered when an integer is passed to Math.ceil through the showBug method. This test case fails because the expectation is that the result should be equal to the input integer value, but it is not due to the bug in the showBug method.
Bug_Trigger_Explanation: The test results show that the test passed without any assertion errors. This means that the output of the showBug method is equal to the input integer value, which is the expected behavior. Since the bug is not triggered, the test results do not confirm the presence of the described bug in the Java code.
